status: frozen before any Stage79 error, fit or score was computed
question: How far should a published general-seat candidate-vote poll move the model's candidate National/Labour balance for that seat, and by how much should it narrow that seat's uncertainty, given the historical error of such polls?

quantity.name: balance
quantity.definition: log(National candidate share / Labour candidate share), the Stage45/47 candidate balance coordinate (log scale; equal to logit of National/(National+Labour))
quantity.pollValue: log(published National share / published Labour share); shares as published, not closed
quantity.modelPrior: centre mu = mean_logit_location(National/(National+Labour) of the conditional mean, total balance SD), the location the bank draws around; Gaussian noise with total SD sigma = hypot(shared, multiplier * seat)

multiplier.source: D107; historical seats use the Stage67 primary flags

eligibility.rule: general seat; the poll publishes both a National and a Labour candidate share; and the poll's two highest published candidate shares are those two candidates
eligibility.consequence: polls led by a Green, ACT or other candidate move no coordinate in this stage (Auckland Central and Wellington Bays in 2026); they stay context
excludedHistorical: Ohariu 2017: the incumbent withdrew after fieldwork (not an error of the poll)

pollError.samplingVariance: 1/(n*pNAT) + 1/(n*pLAB), p = published share / 100, n = published sample size
pollError.inflation: c = max(1, mean over fitting polls of (y - z)^2 / samplingVariance), z the actual balance; one constant, no bias term, no sponsor lean fitted

allowance.note: SD on the log-ratio scale, equal to one typical n=400 sampling SD; a fixed development choice, variance 0.0144; no directional shift

pollError.sameSourceMerge: two polls of one seat by the same pollster within 14 days are merged by inverse variance, the later one with variance multiplied by 1.5 (2026 application only)

update.ageFactor: rho = 0.5 ** (ageWeeks / 6) in the 2026 application; rho = 1 in scoring (the truth is the election result and c absorbs the lag)
update.floor: V' = max(V, sharedSD^2): a seat poll never narrows the shared candidate-split shift (Stage68), so the total seat SD cannot fall below the shared SD
update.assumptions: poll error independent of model error; the seat deviation is stationary AR(1) in time with half-life 6 weeks; national, local-party and Maori layers unchanged

scoring.population: eligible historical polls 2014-2023 for general seats with a Stage44 out-of-sample seat replay
scoring.scheme: leave one seat-election out: c is fitted on the other seat-elections' eligible polls; each poll is scored on its own against the actual balance
metrics: sum of log score difference (modelPlusPoll - model, nats)
mean Gaussian CRPS of each arm
coverage of central 50/80/90 intervals of each arm

adoptionRule.adopt: total leave-one-out log score gain >= 1.0 nat AND modelPlusPoll 80% coverage in [0.65, 0.95]
adoptionRule.otherwise: finding not_established: the 2026 layer stays disabled (seatPolls.enabled false), polls remain context and can still justify a Stage56 exceptional flag or extraSdPp, not both
adoptionRule.biasTerm: none fitted; a Curia/sponsor lean is never adopted by this stage

sensitivities.S1: drop polls whose sample size is assumed
sensitivities.S3: c fitted on every poll that publishes both a National and a Labour share (eligible or not); scoring still on eligible polls

disclosure: Before this freeze the author had computed, from the same Wikipedia tables, a rough log-ratio error for 12 historical polls (root mean square 0.28, sampling floor about 0.12 at n=400) and seen the Stage67 flags; no model-versus-poll comparison had been computed. The fitted c will therefore agree with that crude figure; the test is the leave-one-out comparison, not the error size.
doNot: use party-vote crosstabs from seat polls
change Maori seats, D107 multipliers for unpolled seats, the classification draft or any frozen stage
fit house or sponsor lean, or apply a directional shift to any source
reopen Student-t, mixtures, regimes, sigma shrinkage, geography fragmentation, candidate-quality scores or national MCMC backtest reruns
publish a probability, edit data/sources.json, or enable the 2026 layer unless the adoption rule is met
